items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: And also it’s Dave Whitford on bass and he’s just incredible

ctx.x: I want to ask you about at least one of your compositions that appears on your website, it’s called “Cry.” And it opens with, you know rubato. And I had two questions about it. First of all I think it’s in A flat. And I wondered if you picked that because it allows – because on your tenor you would be in a key that allows for harmonics. It’s helpful to be in that key to play those harmonics you were doing.

Yes. I think that’s in there. It’s also the low B flat as the bottom note and I love that note. And also, just as I was coming up with the first section of the melody, and the high F on tenor is a really nice note, and then it goes up to altissimo B flat. And that just felt quite – it’s quite a raw note, quite gritty, and it seemed to fit the atmosphere of that particular piece which is just really supposed to be very emotional, very raw and not sweet let’s say. So I think that’s why, yeah. And I wrote that,…
